messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a consistent skew between the per-tenant cost numbers in the console and the raw token ledger after we enabled sticky routing for dedicated pools.
devin: sketch it out — what kind of skew and for which routes?
maya: For some high-cache-hit routes the console shows much lower unit cost than ledger implies. Looks like cache credits are being applied at the route aggregation layer but not reflected back to the model/sku breakdown.
sam: that's... expected if attribution happens before routing. We applied cache-crediting at final aggregation to avoid double-crediting when fallback routes hit. but that means per-model cards can look inflated.
elaine: can you paste an example tenant and timeslice? we can diff ledger vs dashboard.
maya: tenant: acme-infra, window: 2026-02-20 08:00-09:00 UTC. quick diff:
```
ledger.tokens: 1,200,000
ledger.cost_usd: 480
console.reported_cost: 320
console.cache_credits: 0.35 (35% assumed)
```
so console shows cost after route-level cache credits but the per-model card still shows raw model spend.
dryn: (note: dynaname) sorry, meant devin.
devin: Ok — sounds like two separate problems: 1) attribution order (when credits applied), 2) telemetry lineage (can't trace which routing decision led to which ledger line).
ryan: I'm worried about quotas too — if console shows lower cost tenant-side they might hit quota limits incorrectly. We need quotas to reflect post-credit tokens or show both. UX question.
maya: Exactly. Product asked for "effective tokens" in billing view. Engineering needs a clear signal to attribute.
sam: proposal: attach a routing_decision_id (RID) to every request in the proxy and emit it into both the ledger and the console aggregation pipeline. that way, cache savings calculated at routing time can be joined back to ledger rows.
elaine: +1 for RID. Also need a deterministic fingerprint for caching: route fingerprint, model_sku, input_prefix_hash.
devin: we already have a request_id; RID is different — it's the chosen route variant after policy. Implementation: proxy emits {request_id, rid, chosen_pool, fallback_reason, cache_hit:true/false} to the telemetry stream.
maya: Will that blow up cardinality in our OLAP? how many unique RIDs?
sam: RIDs are ephemeral but limited: they represent decision trees (e.g., pool-A:quantized, pool-B:default). We can hash to a compact rid tag.
ryan: Quotas: we should compute two numbers: billed_tokens (pre-credit) and effective_tokens (post-credit). Show effective in tenant usage UI, but keep billed in invoices and raw ledger.
elaine: For the dashboard: add a toggle "Show effective cost (after cache)". Default to on for product teams, off for accounting.
maya: rollout implications — for canaries we need to ensure older clients/proxies that don't emit RID don't break joins. join must be resilient.
devin: fallback: join on request_id when RID absent. we should also emit a RID_NULL marker.
sam: Quick implementation plan:
1) proxy: generate rid for every decision, emit to kafka telemetry topic `routing.decisions` and include rid in existing `request.events` topic.
2) ledger: add rid field to per-request rows (nullable)
3) aggregation: run a post-join that computes cache_credit_by_rid and applies credit to per-model and per-route aggregations.
4) console: surface both billed and effective columns + link to "why credit applied" drilldown which shows rid and decisions.
5) backfill: run a join job for last 30 days with best-effort matching on request_id.

devin: timeline? I can own 1+2, sam can help with 3, elaine with console UX and backfill coordination.
sam: I can start the aggregation pipeline change. question: how do we compute credit percentage? current heuristic is prefix-KV reuse rate, but that must be computed at routing time and attached to RID.
maya: Right — router can compute a small stat bundle: {cache_hit_count, tokens_saved_estimate}. emit that with RID.
ryan: Security: rid shouldn't contain PII. make sure we only emit hashed fingerprints.
elaine: UX followups: for rollout, add a subtle badge in the model card when credits exceed X% and a hover explanation.
devin: For canaries: when a new routing policy rolls out, we should label RIDs with policy_version so we can compare effective unit cost across versions.
sam: corner case: multi-stage routing (outer router chooses region, inner chooses quantized variant). RID needs to be composable or a single canonical string representing vector decisions.
maya: I think a stable RID format: `policy:vX|region:us-east-1|pool:q8_deploy` hashed to 16 chars. store both canonical and hashed if needed.
elaine: Need sample payload for the events team. devin can you paste a proto-ish shape?
devin: quick shape:
```
{
  request_id: string,
  rid: string,
  rid_fingerprint: string,
  policy_version: string,
  chosen_pool: string,
  cache_hit: bool,
  tokens_requested: int,
  tokens_served_from_cache: int,
  tokens_billed: int,
  tokens_effective: int, // billed - tokens_served_from_cache or apply quantization factor
  timestamp: iso
}
```
sam: perfect. we should keep tokens_effective nullable until aggregation validates.
maya: Are we happy with the plan? any objections about adding rid to the ledger? that's the crux.
ryan: no objections. ledger schema change needs migration plan but it's minor (nullable string column).
elaine: I'll mock console wireframes after lunch and include effective/billed toggles + rid drilldown UX.
devin: I'll open the PR for telemetry topic schema and add the rid emission in proxy. tagging this for next sprint.
deploy-bot: deploy requested by dev-deployer to infra/proxy at 1749998900 — status: successful :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a cross-team RFC doc and link here.
sam: can we add a small smoke test that asserts effective_tokens <= billed_tokens? helpful guardrail.
devin: yes, I'll add that to the aggregation job.
maya: ok closing this thread, will ping once RFC is up. :thumbsup:
